lines.text: Hi there!
lines.screen: White room, soft floor

lines.text: Quick question.
lines.screen: A question card drops in on a string and swings

lines.text: When you build a website, how do you know it works, and that it's safe, before real people use it?
lines.screen: Card: website icon with a big ?, 'Does it work? Is it safe?'
lines.student: Scratches head, ?! pops over him, then shrugs

lines.text: Let's look at the problem.
lines.screen: Label: The problem
lines.student: Sits down cross-legged, ready to learn

lines.text: Websites break in small ways. A button that does nothing. A checkout that fails. An error that shows secret details.
lines.screen: Three cards pop in one by one: broken button, failed checkout, leaked error
lines.student: Jumps a little at each card

lines.text: And attackers look for exactly these weak spots.
lines.screen: Cards turn red, an eye peeks over them

lines.text: A big 2025 study by Verizon looked at how break-ins usually start.
lines.screen: Bar chart grows out of the floor; the middle bar lifts the student up

lines.text: Stolen passwords. Weak spots in software. And trick emails.
lines.screen: Each bar lights up as it is named: 22, 20 and 16 out of 100
lines.student: Points at each bar from on top

lines.text: And when it goes wrong, it costs a lot.
lines.screen: Bars sink away

lines.text: IBM found that one data breach costs about four point four million dollars on average,
lines.screen: Big counter rolls up to $4.44 million, coins fly

lines.text: and takes around two hundred and forty days to find and stop.
lines.screen: Hourglass and a counter to 241 days

lines.text: Checking everything by hand is slow, and things get missed.
lines.screen: Label: By hand is slow

lines.text: So, what do teams really need?
lines.screen: Label: What teams need
lines.student: Hand on chin, then a lightbulb pops

lines.text: One. Real tests, in a real browser.
lines.screen: Checklist row 1 ticks: real browser

lines.text: Two. Clear proof for every problem, so it's quick to fix.
lines.screen: Row 2 ticks: proof for every problem

lines.text: Three. Safety first. The tester must never become the danger.
lines.screen: Row 3 ticks: safety first

lines.text: Meet AgentGuard!
lines.screen: The AgentGuard card rises from the floor, confetti
lines.student: Lifted up on the card, arms up

lines.text: Your friendly AI tester for websites.
lines.screen: Subtitle on the card
lines.student: Sits on the card, swings his legs

lines.text: Here's how it works.
lines.screen: Label: How it works

lines.text: First, you paste your website link.
lines.screen: A link bar types shop.example.com

lines.text: An AI planner, running on Vultr, writes a test plan.
lines.say: An AI planner, running on Vulture, writes a test plan.
lines.screen: Robot card and a 3-step plan; 'runs on Vultr' tag

lines.text: Then every test runs inside its own safe box, called a sandbox, with a real browser.
lines.screen: Three sandbox boxes drop in, each with a browser
lines.student: Walks over and peeks into a box

lines.text: It checks pages, forms, logins, checkouts, and security settings.
lines.screen: Five check chips tick one by one

lines.text: And if a test ever tries something unsafe,
lines.screen: A red arrow sneaks from a box toward a private cloud

lines.text: it's blocked, written in a log, and that box is thrown away.
lines.screen: STOP sign slams down, log card, the box falls into the bin

lines.text: At the end, you get a clear report. What broke, the proof, and how to fix it.
lines.screen: Report card with three rows

lines.text: Plus one simple answer. Block, fix first, or safe to ship.
lines.screen: Three answer lights glow as they are named

lines.text: AgentGuard. Test it before your users do.
lines.say: Agent Guard. Test it before your users do.
lines.screen: Logo and tagline

lines.text: Built on Vultr.
lines.screen: Built on Vultr badge
